Question: Square \(PQRS\) lies in the first quadrant. Points \((3, 0),\) \((5, 0),\) \((7, 0),\) and \((13, 0)\) lie on lines \(SP,\) \(RQ,\) \(PQ,\) and \(SR,\) respectively. What is the sum of the coordinates of the center of the square \(PQRS?\)
Solution:
Method 1: Method 1: Use similar right triangles

Name the four given axis points \(A=(3,0)\), \(B=(5,0)\), \(C=(7,0)\), and \(D=(13,0)\). The side lines create right triangles with these axis points. Their hypotenuses have known lengths, making similarity useful.

Triangles \(ACP\) and \(BCQ\) are right at \(P\) and \(Q\), respectively. They share the angle at \(C\): the rays \(CA\) and \(CB\) agree, and \(CP\) and \(CQ\) agree because both vertices lie above the axis. Hence they are similar. Since \(AC=4\) and \(BC=2\),
\[
CP=2CQ,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad PQ=CQ.
\]
Likewise, right triangles \(BDR\) and \(BCQ\) share the angle at \(B\). The rays \(BR\) and \(BQ\) agree because both vertices lie above the axis. Since \(BD=8=4BC\),
\[
BR=4BQ,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad QR=3BQ.
\]
The square has \(PQ=QR\), so \(CQ=3BQ\).

Let \(BQ=t>0\). In right triangle \(BQC\), the hypotenuse is \(BC=2\), so
\[
t^2+(3t)^2=2^2,
\qquad t^2=\frac25.
\]
Let \(H\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(Q\) to \(BC\). Similarity of triangles \(BHQ\) and \(BQC\) gives
\[
BH=\frac{BQ^2}{BC}=\frac15,
\qquad
QH=\frac{BQ\cdot CQ}{BC}=\frac35.
\]
Thus \(Q=(26/5,3/5)\). Since \(Q\) is the midpoint of \(CP\), and \(BR=4BQ\),
\[
P=\left(\frac{17}{5},\frac65\right),
\qquad
R=\left(\frac{29}{5},\frac{12}{5}\right).
\]
The center is the midpoint of diagonal \(PR\), namely \((23/5,9/5)\). Its coordinate sum is
\[
\frac{23}{5}+\frac95=\boxed{6.4},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

Method 2: Method 2: Equate the distances between opposite sides

No side line can be horizontal: a horizontal line through one of the given points would be the \(x\)-axis, contradicting the square's first-quadrant location. A vertical side would force an adjacent horizontal side, so all side slopes are finite and nonzero.

Let \(SP\) have slope \(m\ne0\). Opposite sides are parallel, and adjacent sides are perpendicular, so the given intercepts give the equations
\[
\begin{aligned}
SP:&\quad mx-y=3m, & RQ:&\quad mx-y=5m,\\
PQ:&\quad x+my=7, & SR:&\quad x+my=13.
\end{aligned}
\]
The distance between parallel lines \(ax+by=c_1\) and \(ax+by=c_2\) is \(|c_1-c_2|/\sqrt{a^2+b^2}\). Each opposite-side distance equals the square's side length. Therefore
\[
\frac{2|m|}{\sqrt{m^2+1}}
=\frac6{\sqrt{m^2+1}},
\qquad |m|=3.
\]
Write the center as \((h,k)\). It lies halfway between each pair of opposite sides, so
\[
mh-k=4m,
\qquad h+mk=10.
\]
Multiplying the second equation by \(m\) and subtracting the first gives
\[
(m^2+1)k=6m.
\]
Since \(k>0\), we must have \(m>0\), selecting \(m=3\). The center equations then yield \(k=9/5\) and \(h=23/5\). Hence
\[
h+k=\frac{32}{5}=\boxed{6.4},
\]
choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
